Login or signup to continue reading All articles from our website The digital version of Today's Paper All other regional websites in your area Continue 2 stars The 90s were the best period for domestic thrillers. You had the number one, the one that put the phrase 'bunny boiler' into popular culture: Fatal Attraction . There was Julia Roberts vehicle Sleeping with the Enemy , Bridget Fonda's Single White Female and (if we can stretch the 90s to 2000) Michelle Pfeiffer's brilliant What Lies Beneath . And, of course, the film that made people suspicious of nannies forever: The Hand that Rocks the Cradle . Each of these films so brilliantly distills a very real threat that can't be escaped, because it's inside the home. And they all have iconic performances. That makes reimagining them a difficult ask. Fatal Attraction has been attempted with a relatively well-received series starring Joshua Jackson and Lizzy Caplan. Maika Monroe and Mary Elizabeth Winstead in The Hand that Rocks the Cradle. Picture Disney+ And now The Hand that Rocks the Cradle has been reimagined as a new film. It's not a straight remake, as the characters and scenario are different, but it has the same basic skeleton of the original. Mary Elizabeth Winstead ( 10 Cloverfield Lane ) is mum of two Caitlyn Morales, who is convinced by her husband Miguel (Raul Castillo, Task ) to hire a nanny to help her out with the new baby as she struggled with post-partum difficulties following the birth of their first child, daughter Emma (Mileiah Vega). As luck would have it, Caitlyn runs into Polly (Maika Monroe, Longlegs ) - who she had briefly met months earlier - at a farmer's market and soon after she's moved into the Morales' house as a live-in nanny. It's clear pretty early that Polly doesn't exactly have the family's best wishes at heart, and pulls various stunts to drive wedges between Caitlyn and her husband and daughter. Where this film succeeds is in playing on Caitlyn's fears that she's not a good enough mother. Polly arranges situations, big and small, that make Caitlyn question her parenting skills, and she starts doubting the reality around her. Gaslighting to a tee. Polly is great at picking up family dynamics and pushing just the right buttons to make everything fall apart. The original film featured Solomon, a character played by Ernie Hudson, who did various handyman tasks around the house for the family. He was part of a disability employment organisation, and while it's not explicitly stated, his character displayed signs of having autism. It's not the most sensitive portrayal of a character with autism and he's not treated especially well by the script, even if he is ultimately allowed to be heroic. A character like Solomon would not be warmly received in today's climate, especially if played by somebody who was not on the spectrum themselves, and as such he has no counterpart in the new The Hand that Rocks the Cradle . Narratively though, Solomon is missed. The story needs someone who sees what the nefarious nanny is up to but is silenced. We sort of get that through the couple's friend Stewart (Martin Starr, Freaks and Geeks ), but he's much more of a parallel to Julianne Moore's character from the original than Hudson's. And in that respect, he certainly doesn't have the impact Moore did. Winstead and Monroe are both excellent. The former has a great grip on showing just the right amount of growing paranoia, and is at all times believable. Monroe also has an incredible deadness behind her eyes and you start to question why anyone would let her be alone with their children. Speaking of children, young Vega is also impressive as Emma. In removing the prologue sequence from the original film, some of the motivations that were evident the entire time in 1992 are delivered as a shock reveal in 2025 (and it is a shock, because the motivations are not the same), and that's a tick in the positive column for this film. The new film also has some shocking moments of blood and gore which help elevate it's Halloween-month release credentials. But overall, as far as pure entertainment value goes, the original The Hand that Rocks the Cradle is far superior to its reimagination. The tension and thrills that made the original so great, and the unhinged nature of Rebecca de Mornay's nanny, are nowhere to be found here, and that's a real shame. Login or signup to continue reading All articles from our website The digital version of Today's Paper All other regional websites in your area Continue 2 stars The 90s were the best period for domestic thrillers. You had the number one, the one that put the phrase 'bunny boiler' into popular culture: Fatal Attraction . There was Julia Roberts vehicle Sleeping with the Enemy , Bridget Fonda's Single White Female and (if we can stretch the 90s to 2000) Michelle Pfeiffer's brilliant What Lies Beneath . And, of course, the film that made people suspicious of nannies forever: The Hand that Rocks the Cradle . Each of these films so brilliantly distills a very real threat that can't be escaped, because it's inside the home. And they all have iconic performances. That makes reimagining them a difficult ask. Fatal Attraction has been attempted with a relatively well-received series starring Joshua Jackson and Lizzy Caplan. Maika Monroe and Mary Elizabeth Winstead in The Hand that Rocks the Cradle. Picture Disney+ And now The Hand that Rocks the Cradle has been reimagined as a new film. It's not a straight remake, as the characters and scenario are different, but it has the same basic skeleton of the original. Mary Elizabeth Winstead ( 10 Cloverfield Lane ) is mum of two Caitlyn Morales, who is convinced by her husband Miguel (Raul Castillo, Task ) to hire a nanny to help her out with the new baby as she struggled with post-partum difficulties following the birth of their first child, daughter Emma (Mileiah Vega). As luck would have it, Caitlyn runs into Polly (Maika Monroe, Longlegs ) - who she had briefly met months earlier - at a farmer's market and soon after she's moved into the Morales' house as a live-in nanny. It's clear pretty early that Polly doesn't exactly have the family's best wishes at heart, and pulls various stunts to drive wedges between Caitlyn and her husband and daughter. Where this film succeeds is in playing on Caitlyn's fears that she's not a good enough mother. Polly arranges situations, big and small, that make Caitlyn question her parenting skills, and she starts doubting the reality around her. Gaslighting to a tee. Polly is great at picking up family dynamics and pushing just the right buttons to make everything fall apart. The original film featured Solomon, a character played by Ernie Hudson, who did various handyman tasks around the house for the family. He was part of a disability employment organisation, and while it's not explicitly stated, his character displayed signs of having autism. It's not the most sensitive portrayal of a character with autism and he's not treated especially well by the script, even if he is ultimately allowed to be heroic. A character like Solomon would not be warmly received in today's climate, especially if played by somebody who was not on the spectrum themselves, and as such he has no counterpart in the new The Hand that Rocks the Cradle . Narratively though, Solomon is missed. The story needs someone who sees what the nefarious nanny is up to but is silenced. We sort of get that through the couple's friend Stewart (Martin Starr, Freaks and Geeks ), but he's much more of a parallel to Julianne Moore's character from the original than Hudson's. And in that respect, he certainly doesn't have the impact Moore did. Winstead and Monroe are both excellent. The former has a great grip on showing just the right amount of growing paranoia, and is at all times believable. Monroe also has an incredible deadness behind her eyes and you start to question why anyone would let her be alone with their children. Speaking of children, young Vega is also impressive as Emma. In removing the prologue sequence from the original film, some of the motivations that were evident the entire time in 1992 are delivered as a shock reveal in 2025 (and it is a shock, because the motivations are not the same), and that's a tick in the positive column for this film. The new film also has some shocking moments of blood and gore which help elevate it's Halloween-month release credentials. But overall, as far as pure entertainment value goes, the original The Hand that Rocks the Cradle is far superior to its reimagination. The tension and thrills that made the original so great, and the unhinged nature of Rebecca de Mornay's nanny, are nowhere to be found here, and that's a real shame. Presley, the only child of Elvis and Priscilla Presley , died suddenly age 54 in January 2023 from a small bowel obstruction caused by complications from bariatric surgery. She left behind three children — daughter Riley, 36, whom she shared with ex-husband Danny Keough, and 17-year-old twins Harper and Finley with ex-husband Michael Lockwood — as well as the memory of her late son Benjamin, who died by suicide in 2020 at age 27. In the wake of her death, a bitter legal battle erupted between Riley and her grandmother Priscilla over control of Lisa Marie’s estate. Though the dispute was eventually settled, Priscilla has since become entangled in a financial feud with former advisers — one that’s turned ugly , with an explosive allegation that she prematurely \'pulled the plug\' on her daughter. Now, as she releases the paperback edition of her memoir From Here to the Great Unknown, Riley says her mother has made her presence known. Keough told People in 2024 that her mother really died from a broken heart, after her brother brother Benjamin died by suicide. In 2022, Lisa Marie admitted that she would never \'move on\' from her son\'s death, with Riley revealing in her memoir that Lisa Marie and her started to move on by helping others. \'One kid wrote to Riley and said, "I didn’t kill myself last night because of what you said it would do to my family and those that are left behind. By Kyle Smith Share Resize Listen (5 min) Adults who complain that they want more theatrical movies that aren’t silly spectacles involving capes, spandex and or/aliens firing death rays have only themselves to blame: There are still plenty of features about recognizable human dilemmas, but none of them are selling tickets anymore. It wasn’t so long ago that indies such as 2016’s “Manchester by the Sea” (domestic box office: $48 million) and 2017’s “Lady Bird” ($49 million) and “The Big Sick” ($43 million) drew large and appreciative audiences to theaters. This year, by sad contrast, such highly touted films as “The Life of Chuck,” “After the Hunt” and “If I Had Legs I’d Kick You” fell well short of $10 million in domestic sales. Whenever I meet people over 40 who find out I’m a film critic, the first thing they always tell me is, “I can’t remember the last time I went out to a theater.” Lots of people under 25 still go, however, and that’s why virtually everything is aimed at them. Still, most character-based, reality-grounded dramas and comedies are just as good on the small screen, where most of my picks quickly went. Some were even made by streaming services, notably my favorite release of 2025, “Jay Kelly” (on Netflix Dec. 5), Noah Baumbach’s dramedy in which a dream cast headed by George Clooney and Adam Sandler balances mockery of showbiz follies with a gentle acceptance of the bizarre circumstances that screen superstars must navigate. As the eponymous figure, a global Hollywood icon, Mr. Clooney is obtuse yet endearing as his character tries to reconnect with his young-adult daughter on a jaunt through Europe to an Italian film festival. Mr. Sandler, as his perpetually suffering manager and sort-of friend, is equally tender and funny, while the glorious supporting cast includes Billy Crudup , Jim Broadbent , Laura Dern and Riley Keough . Staff Picks BY Alex Hudson Published Nov 13, 2025 I can\'t remember the previous time a song gave me a genuine jump scare — but I certainly remember the latest time, since it happened a few seconds ago: Tobias Jesso Jr. \'s "I Love You" freaked the shit out of me! Let me set the scene: I\'m visiting my mom on the West Coast but maintaining Toronto hours while working from here, so I was the only one awake while working in a dark house this morning. On my headphones, I turned on "I Love You" — the songwriter\'s first solo release in 10 years, following a decade spent as a Grammy-winning songwriter for the biggest pop artists in the world (Adele, Justin Bieber, Harry Styles, etc.). The song is a quiet, Beatles-y piano ballad — very pretty, but several notches more restrained than, say, Adele\'s "When We Were Young." Or so I thought, until the 2:51 mark, when THWACK , an enormous drum beat absolutely obliterates the mix. To my untrained ears, it seems to have sidechain compression, with the rest of the track ducking queasily under the sound of the chaotic percussion, which smashes through the arrangement like a bull in a china shop. For a guy known as a pop songwriter, this song follows a very different path, finding its footing with an ostentatious production choice rather than relatable songwriting content. I assumed the drums were chopped up on a computer, but the video (which features Dakota Johnson and Riley Keough just sitting there, seemingly for no reason than to add a little star power) reveals that the whole thing was played live with a drummer. It\'s quite an introduction to s h i n e , the long-awaited follow-up to 2015\'s Goon , which arrives November 21 on R&R . The Academy of Motion Pictures Arts and Sciences and Chanel hosted what has become an annual luncheon for women who act, write, direct, produce, and take part in numerous aspects of filmmaking at the Academy Museum on Tuesday, November 4. The midday gathering brought together those who have received Oscars and emerging creatives alike to celebrate their collective work and advocate for new projects. “Women make up more than half the population, so anytime you’re interested in telling stories of the majority of the people who are walking on the planet and amplifying their experiences as human beings will always be a worthy way to spend your time,” said Sarah Paulson. Academy President Lynette Howell Taylor welcomed a starry group that also included Kristen Stewart, Zoey Deutch, Patty Jenkins, Felicity Jones, Leslie Mann, Tessa Thompson, Diane Warren, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Riley Keough, Emma Mackey, Maude Apatow, Colleen Atwood, and Kaitlyn Dever. When Black Panther costume designer Ruth E. Carter took the stage, she acknowledged the help she received when she began what became a storied career that now spans more than 50 films. “I wouldn’t be standing here today with two Oscars without people who guided me,” she said, crediting a college professor as well as directors Spike Lee and John Singleton for giving her room to learn and grow. She presented Gold Fellowships to recipients Alina Simone, a Ukrainian-born American journalist and filmmaker whose work has appeared in The New York Times , NPR, The Guardian , The Atlantic , and various film festivals, and Marlén Viñayo, a documentary maker who is based in El Salvador and won the prize as an international filmmaker. Actor and The Chronology of Water director Stewart gave the luncheon’s keynote speech. “In supporting women in film, we’re starting to redefine desire and make films from the places that we really want to come from,” she said, noting how challenging it can be for those who take up the mantle. “I can now attest to the bare-knuckle brawling that it takes every step of the way,” she added. Stewart advocated for films about all the varying elements of women’s complex lives. “Observations about experiences routinely experienced by women frequently provoke disgust and rejection, but they are true so I think that we should tell them.” She finished her speech with a reminder that there are so many more stories to tell: “Those of us who have been lucky enough to make a movie have a responsibility to those who are yet to come.” Dylan Meyer, Kristen Stewart. Presley, the only child of Elvis and Priscilla Presley , died suddenly age 54 in January 2023 from a small bowel obstruction caused by complications from bariatric surgery. She left behind three children — daughter Riley, 36, whom she shared with ex-husband Danny Keough, and 17-year-old twins Harper and Finley with ex-husband Michael Lockwood — as well as the memory of her late son Benjamin, who died by suicide in 2020 at age 27. In the wake of her death, a bitter legal battle erupted between Riley and her grandmother Priscilla over control of Lisa Marie’s estate. Though the dispute was eventually settled, Priscilla has since become entangled in a financial feud with former advisers — one that’s turned ugly , with an explosive allegation that she prematurely \'pulled the plug\' on her daughter. Now, as she releases the paperback edition of her memoir From Here to the Great Unknown, Riley says her mother has made her presence known. That otherworldly connection isn’t new for Riley — she\'s previously said she somehow knew her mother had died before she was officially told . \'I just had a feeling. I don’t know,\' the Daisy Jones and The Six star told Drew Barrymore in October 2024. \'There had been incidents before, you know, health incidents and I didn’t have the same feeling.\' She continued: \'I felt this sort of surrender in the moment and I just had a little bit of a sense.\' Although Presley’s autopsy later revealed she died from a \'small bowel obstruction\' caused by complications from bariatric surgery , Keough previously said she believes her mother’s real cause of death was heartbreak. Keough told People in 2024 that her mother really died from a broken heart, after her brother brother Benjamin died by suicide. There are certainly moments that are very... too weird to not be something,\' she added; (Lisa Marie Presley, Priscilla Presley, and Riley Keough attend the Handprint Ceremony honoring Three Generations of Presley\'s at TCL Chinese Theatre on June 21, 2022) \'My mom tried her best to find strength for me and my younger sisters after Ben died, but we knew how much pain she was in,\' Keough said at the time. \'My mom physically died from the after effects of her surgery, but we all knew she died of a broken heart,\' she said. In 2022, Lisa Marie admitted that she would never \'move on\' from her son\'s death, with Riley revealing in her memoir that Lisa Marie and her started to move on by helping others. \'One kid wrote to Riley and said, "I didn’t kill myself last night because of what you said it would do to my family and those that are left behind. So thank you." That helped me. That brought me up,\' Lisa Marie wrote in the memoir. Riley added that the 2016 Nick Cave documentary One More Time With Feeling also helped immensely, calling it, \'a really beautiful portrayal of grief.\' Benjamin died in July 2020, following an argument with his girlfriend at the family’s mansion. An autopsy later revealed he had both cocaine and alcohol in his system. According to reports, Benjamin had struggled with his mental health for years — he attempted to take his life six months earlier and had entered rehab multiple times, including a three-week stay just four months before his death. By Kyle Smith Share Resize Listen (5 min) Adults who complain that they want more theatrical movies that aren’t silly spectacles involving capes, spandex and or/aliens firing death rays have only themselves to blame: There are still plenty of features about recognizable human dilemmas, but none of them are selling tickets anymore. It wasn’t so long ago that indies such as 2016’s “Manchester by the Sea” (domestic box office: $48 million) and 2017’s “Lady Bird” ($49 million) and “The Big Sick” ($43 million) drew large and appreciative audiences to theaters. This year, by sad contrast, such highly touted films as “The Life of Chuck,” “After the Hunt” and “If I Had Legs I’d Kick You” fell well short of $10 million in domestic sales. Whenever I meet people over 40 who find out I’m a film critic, the first thing they always tell me is, “I can’t remember the last time I went out to a theater.” Lots of people under 25 still go, however, and that’s why virtually everything is aimed at them. Still, most character-based, reality-grounded dramas and comedies are just as good on the small screen, where most of my picks quickly went. Some were even made by streaming services, notably my favorite release of 2025, “Jay Kelly” (on Netflix Dec. 5), Noah Baumbach’s dramedy in which a dream cast headed by George Clooney and Adam Sandler balances mockery of showbiz follies with a gentle acceptance of the bizarre circumstances that screen superstars must navigate. As the eponymous figure, a global Hollywood icon, Mr. Clooney is obtuse yet endearing as his character tries to reconnect with his young-adult daughter on a jaunt through Europe to an Italian film festival. Mr. Sandler, as his perpetually suffering manager and sort-of friend, is equally tender and funny, while the glorious supporting cast includes Billy Crudup , Jim Broadbent , Laura Dern and Riley Keough . Staff Picks BY Alex Hudson Published Nov 13, 2025 I can\'t remember the previous time a song gave me a genuine jump scare — but I certainly remember the latest time, since it happened a few seconds ago: Tobias Jesso Jr. \'s "I Love You" freaked the shit out of me! Let me set the scene: I\'m visiting my mom on the West Coast but maintaining Toronto hours while working from here, so I was the only one awake while working in a dark house this morning. On my headphones, I turned on "I Love You" — the songwriter\'s first solo release in 10 years, following a decade spent as a Grammy-winning songwriter for the biggest pop artists in the world (Adele, Justin Bieber, Harry Styles, etc.). The song is a quiet, Beatles-y piano ballad — very pretty, but several notches more restrained than, say, Adele\'s "When We Were Young." Or so I thought, until the 2:51 mark, when THWACK , an enormous drum beat absolutely obliterates the mix. To my untrained ears, it seems to have sidechain compression, with the rest of the track ducking queasily under the sound of the chaotic percussion, which smashes through the arrangement like a bull in a china shop. For a guy known as a pop songwriter, this song follows a very different path, finding its footing with an ostentatious production choice rather than relatable songwriting content. I assumed the drums were chopped up on a computer, but the video (which features Dakota Johnson and Riley Keough just sitting there, seemingly for no reason than to add a little star power) reveals that the whole thing was played live with a drummer. It\'s quite an introduction to s h i n e , the long-awaited follow-up to 2015\'s Goon , which arrives November 21 on R&R . The Academy of Motion Pictures Arts and Sciences and Chanel hosted what has become an annual luncheon for women who act, write, direct, produce, and take part in numerous aspects of filmmaking at the Academy Museum on Tuesday, November 4. The midday gathering brought together those who have received Oscars and emerging creatives alike to celebrate their collective work and advocate for new projects. “Women make up more than half the population, so anytime you’re interested in telling stories of the majority of the people who are walking on the planet and amplifying their experiences as human beings will always be a worthy way to spend your time,” said Sarah Paulson. She presented Gold Fellowships to recipients Alina Simone, a Ukrainian-born American journalist and filmmaker whose work has appeared in The New York Times , NPR, The Guardian , The Atlantic , and various film festivals, and Marlén Viñayo, a documentary maker who is based in El Salvador and won the prize as an international filmmaker. Actor and The Chronology of Water director Stewart gave the luncheon’s keynote speech. “In supporting women in film, we’re starting to redefine desire and make films from the places that we really want to come from,” she said, noting how challenging it can be for those who take up the mantle. “I can now attest to the bare-knuckle brawling that it takes every step of the way,” she added. The acclaimed actress recently revealed that what followed were offers that were nowhere close to what she was expecting. Lupita Nyong’o details roles she was offered after winning Oscar for 12 Years a Slave Despite winning an Oscar and gaining immense critical acclaim for her performance in her first film, the Black Panther star received offers for stereotypical roles in the industry, shedding light on the existing bias. Lupita Nyong’o discussed the same with Grammy-winning musician Angélique Kidjo in a recent CNN Inside Africa interview . “It really did set the paces for everything I’ve done since,” she said about her role in 12 Years a Slave. “But you know what’s interesting is that, after I won that Academy Award, you’d think, ‘Oh, I’m gonna get lead roles here and there.’ [Instead, it was], ‘Oh, Lupita, we’d like you to play another movie where you’re a slave, but this time you’re on a slave ship.’” Lupita Nyong\'o talks about the role offers she received after winning an Oscar "Oh, Lupita, we\'d like you to play another movie where you\'re a slave, but this time, you\'re on a slave ship." pic.twitter.com/QUf9H6318E — Blackish Press (@blackishpress) November 22, 2025 Nyong’o added, “Those are the kind of offers I was getting in the months after winning my Academy Award.” The Us actress also called this a “tender time” as the media extrapolated on her Hollywood trajectory. She stated, “There were think pieces about: ‘Is this the beginning and end of this dark-skinned Black African woman’s career?’ I had to deafen myself to all those pontificators because, at the end of the day, I’m not a theory; I’m an actual person.” Moreover, Lupita Nyong’o divulged how her goal was to broaden the scope of African storytelling, but it always came attached with stereotypes. “I like to be a joyful warrior for changing the paradigms of what it means to be African, and if that means that I work one job less a year to ensure that I’m not perpetuating the stereotypes that are expected of people from my continent, then let me do that,” she added. Meanwhile, the 42-year-old actress will soon appear in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey . Lupita Nyong’o is getting real about her acting career since winning an Oscar in 2013 for 12 Years A Slave . The acclaimed actress, who won the Academy Award for her captivating performance as enslaved woman Patsey, told CNN Inside Africa about how she only received offers for similar roles yet refused to play into the stereotypes. View this post on Instagram A post shared by CNN Africa (@cnnafrica) “My winning an Academy Award came at the very start of my career,” Nyong’o, 42, said. “It was for the first film I had ever done. So, it really did set the paces for everything I’ve done since. What’s very interesting is that after I won the Academy Award, you’d think like, ‘Oh, I’m going to get the lead roles here and there.’ But it’s ‘Oh, Lupita. We’d like you to do another movie where you’re a slave, but this time you’re on a slave ship.’ Those are the kinds of offers [I was getting] in the months after winning my Academy Award.” As others began to notice her name on fewer movie posters, Nyong’o had to block out the noise. She remained adamant about following her heart and mind by choosing roles she felt aligned with her values. She even called the moment immediately after winning a “very tender time.” “There is an expectation for you and your career,” she continued. “There were think pieces about, is this the beginning or the end of this African woman’s career? I had to deafen myself to all those pontificators because at the end of the day I am not a theory…I am an actual person. I like to be a joyful warrior for changing the paradigms of what it means to be African. If that means I work one less job a year to ensure that I am not perpetuating these stereotypes that are expected of people from my content, then let me do that.” She still starred in some Blockbuster hits such as Star Wars: The Force Awakens and Black Panther. However, fans also saw her take on more culturally-enriching roles in films like Queen of Katwe . However, Hollywood pressure still got to the Us actress. Last year, she told Trevor Noah on his What Now ? podcast about her subconscious decision to lose her Kenyan accent to appeal to the American film market. Her plight is a similar experience many Black actors in Hollywood have felt before. With pay gaps and a lack of opportunities besides stereotypical roles, Black actors have voiced the fight for just and equitable representation in films. More sure of her art and voice today, Nyong’o is reaffirming her pride in her Kenyan-Mexican identity and face as a Black actress in Hollywood. She will grace the big screen again in Christopher Nolan’s upcoming blockbuster adaptation of The Odyssey. Bassyonni 27 Nov 2025 Home News Sports Entertainment Tech Business Home Entertainment Lupita Nyong’o Celebrates Chadwick Boseman’s Regal Walk of Fame Star Entertainment Lupita Nyong’o Celebrates Chadwick Boseman’s Regal Walk of Fame Star Bassyonni ago 7 days On November 20, 2023, Chadwick Boseman will be honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, highlighting his substantial contributions to film and culture. This tribute comes more than three years after his untimely death on August 28, 2020, due to colon cancer at the age of 43. Lupita Nyong’o Reflects on Boseman’s Legacy Lupita Nyong’o, Boseman’s co-star in the groundbreaking film “Black Panther,” expressed her reverence for the actor. She remarked that having his star near the Dolby Theatre signifies a space of prominence for a true king. “It means it won’t be missed,” she stated, emphasizing the importance of his legacy. Cultural Impact of “Black Panther” “Black Panther,” released in January 2018, was a cultural phenomenon and the first superhero film to earn a Best Picture nomination at the Academy Awards. The film grossed over $1.3 billion globally, showcasing the significance of African representation in Hollywood. Release Date: January 2018 Box Office Gross: $1.3 billion Awards: First superhero film nominated for Best Picture Boseman portrayed T’Challa, the regal superhero from Wakanda, symbolizing strength and pride in African ancestry. His performances as historical figures, including Jackie Robinson and Thurgood Marshall, further showcased his depth as an actor. Boseman’s Private Struggles and Public Philanthropy Boseman kept his battle with cancer private. Many of his colleagues, including Nyong’o and director Ryan Coogler, were unaware of his condition. Despite the challenges he faced, Boseman continued to work on significant projects, leaving an indelible mark on the film industry. Outside his film performances, Boseman was known for his charitable work. He visited pediatric cancer patients even while fighting his own illness, demonstrating his commitment to helping others. Commemoration and Memorials In recognition of his contributions, several memorials have been established. Howard University has reestablished its school of fine arts in Boseman’s name, and a performing arts academy in his hometown, Anderson, South Carolina, also honors him. The upcoming Hollywood Walk of Fame star will serve as another location for fans and admirers to pay their respects. Howard University: School of fine arts renamed in his honor Anderson, SC: Performing arts academy named after Boseman Lupita Nyong’o captures Boseman’s essence well when recalling his impactful presence both on and off the screen. She noted, “There was something about him that you couldn’t explain why he moved you so much.” His legacy, marked by both his artistic achievements and personal character, continues to resonate deeply with audiences worldwide. Conclusion Chadwick Boseman’s star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame will serve as a lasting tribute to his remarkable life and work. Photo: AP You have probably heard his name many times this past week on social media or the news – but if you missed it, 34-year-old Zohran Mamdani recently won New York City’s mayoral election after a smart, engaging, long-running campaign. Given the buzz surrounding his historic rise to be the Big Apple’s new mayor, a lot of stories and claims have emerged. One of these claims is that Mamdani was once a rapper before entering politics. Is this true? VERDICT: TRUE Yes, this is true. Mamdani pursued rapping as a career for a time as “Young Cardamom” which later became “Mr Cardamom.” He released his first song in 2016, collaborating with Ugandan rapper HAB on “Kanda (Chap Chap)”, a track about chapatti that became a local hit. They then released an EP titled “Sidda Mukyaalo” - translated as "No going back to the village" - which explored themes of postcolonial identity and multicultural belonging. Nani, released in 2019, was his final single before entering politics. The song was a tribute to his grandmother, Praveen Nair. On rapping, Mamdani said that music was his way to explore heritage and belonging. Aside from music, Mamdani also worked as a music supervisor on his mother Mira Nair’s 2016 film “Queen of Katwe” which starred Lupita Nyong’o and David Oyelowo. "I do feel like only through writing the book have I gotten to a place where I think there might be a way of exploring acting that doesn\'t carry that baggage that I carried with me for so long," she told E! News in October 2022. "Maybe if I write something for myself. I think that\'d really be maybe one of the only ways I could kind of try exploring it again." Tim Rooke/Shutterstock Meghan Markle This felt like something of a no-brainer. If we had a shot to marry Prince Harry , dedicate our life to the philanthropic causes that matter most to us and gain access to the Queen\'s impressive collection of tiaras, bidding ta-ta to Tinseltown would feel like an okay sacrifice. Following the path Grace Kelly took from Hollywood to the Palace of Monaco, Meghan left behind her home in Toronto—and her breakout role on Suits —for a life in The Firm. Though, now that she and Harry have shed their senior roles and live in Montecito, Calif., she\'s edging back into the business thanks to business moves like their multi-year production deal with Netflix . The Duchess of Sussex released her 2022 docuseries Harry & Meghan as well as her 2025 lifestyle show With Love, Meghan on the streaming service. She\'s also launched podcasts and her brand As Ever. Matthias Nareyek/Getty Images Cameron Diaz Having made upwards of 40 movies since her debut in 1994\'s The Mask , the actress was long overdue for a break when filming wrapped on 2014\'s Annie . "I just decided that I wanted different things out of my life," she explained to pal Gwyneth Paltrow of her ultimate act of self-care. "I had gone so hard for so long, working, making films and it\'s such a grind. When you\'re making a movie—it\'s a perfect excuse—they own you. You\'re there for 12 hours a day for months on end and you have no time for anything else." And there was plenty more she\'d like to explore, from writing (she followed up her 2013 New York Times best-seller The Body Book with 2016\'s The Longevity Book ) to starting a family with husband Benji Madden . But while Cameron confessed to InStyle in 2019, "I don\'t miss performing. Right now I\'m looking at the landscape of wellness and all that," apparently she could be swayed into making at least one encore. "We just begged and pleased on my knees, like, \'Just give the people one more again,\'" Jamie Foxx told E! News of getting Cameron to sign on for the 2025 Netflix film Back in Action . "We love her, we\'ve been waiting on her and this is just gonna be fantastic." John Lamparski/Getty Images Terrence Howard The actor insisted there\'d be no encore after he finished his five-year run on Empire . When Extra asked Terrence about his future ahead of the musical drama series\' sixth and final season in 2019, he responded, "Oh, I\'m done with acting. I\'m done pretending." And though he returned to set for a handful of projects, the Oscar nominee again announced his plans to quit acting while promoting his Peacock series The Best Man: The Final Chapters in 2022. "I\'ve gotten to the point where now I\'ve given the very best that I have as an actor," he told ET . "Now I\'m enjoying watching other new talent come around, and I don\'t want to do an impersonation of myself." Despite these comments, though, Howard has since appeared in a few more shows and movies, including the TV series Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist and Netflix film Shirley , with multiple projects lined up in the future. Andrew H. Walker/Variety/REX/Shutterstock Jack Gleeson Once his time as King Joffrey came to a sudden, purple-faced end in 2014, the then-21-year-old told EW he was getting out of the game. "I\'ve been acting since age 8," the Game of Thrones star explained of his decision. "I just stopped enjoying it as much as I used to." No longer a child star, a bit of the magic had worn off. "Now there\'s the prospect of doing it for a living, whereas up until now it was always something I did for recreation with my friends, or in the summer for some fun," Jack continued. "I enjoyed it. When you make a living from something, it changes your relationship with it. It\'s not like I hate it, it\'s just not what I want to do." But after a six-year break, he was ready to resume his reign , joining the cast of BBC\'s series Out of Her Mind in 2020. Since then, Jack has also appeared in movies like Rebecca\'s Boyfriend and In the Land of Saints and Sinners as well as TV shows like Safe Harbor and The Famous Five . Frazer Harrison/Getty Images Phoebe Cates When Fast Times at Ridgemont High \'s dream girl ( Jennifer Aniston took on her part in September 2020\'s virtual table read ) wed fellow actor Kevin Kline in 1989, they "agreed to alternate so that we\'re never working at the same time," he told Playboy of their plan to care for son Owen and daughter Greta (a singer who now goes by the stage name Frankie Cosmos ). However, he continued, "whenever it\'s been her slot to work, Phoebe has chosen to stay with the children." Though she made a cameo in pal Jennifer Jason Leigh \'s 2001 indie The Anniversary Party , Cates devotes most of her time to operating her New York City boutique Blue Tree . Jamie McCarthy/WireImage Rick Moranis At the height of his Ghostbusters and Honey, I ... fame, the \'80s star stepped away from filmmaking not long after his wife passed away from breast cancer in 1991 to focus on raising his kids Rachel and Mitchell. Though Rick hasn\'t had a live-action movie role since 1997, even passing on a cameo in Paul Feig \'s 2016 Ghostbusters remake, he\'s remained a treasured cultural icon, as evidenced by the outrage over reports that he\'d been assaulted while walking in New York City in 2020. Thankfully there\'s good news for fans: He\'ll make his triumphant return alongside Josh Gad in the forthcoming Disney reboot Shrunk . Larry Busacca/Getty Images Leelee Sobieski Once she wed fashion designer Adam Kimmel in 2010, the Never Been Kissed standout hinted that she was maybe kinda done with movies. "Ninety percent of acting roles involve so much sexual stuff with other people, and I don\'t want to do that," she explained to Vogue . "It\'s such a strange fire to play with, and our relationship is surely strong enough to handle it, but if you\'re going to walk through fire, there has to be something incredible on the other side." Her decision was solidified after son Martin joined older sister Louisanna in 2014. "I don\'t do movie stuff anymore. I am totally an outsider! I think that\'s mainly why I stopped." Rob Latour/Shutterstock Portia de Rossi She\'d done Ally McBeal . And Nip/Tuck . Then Arrested Development and finally Scandal when the Aussie realized that maybe she was ready to turn the dial . "I was approaching 45 and I just kind of…was wondering is there something that I could tackle now that I\'ve never done before that would be really challenging and different," she explained on wife Ellen DeGeneres \' eponymous talk show in 2018. "I kind of knew what acting would look like for me for the next 10, 20 years, so I decided to quit and start a business." The acclaimed actress recently revealed that what followed were offers that were nowhere close to what she was expecting. Lupita Nyong’o discussed the same with Grammy-winning musician Angélique Kidjo in a recent CNN Inside Africa interview . “It really did set the paces for everything I’ve done since,” she said about her role in 12 Years a Slave. “But you know what’s interesting is that, after I won that Academy Award, you’d think, ‘Oh, I’m gonna get lead roles here and there.’ [Instead, it was], ‘Oh, Lupita, we’d like you to play another movie where you’re a slave, but this time you’re on a slave ship.’” Lupita Nyong\'o talks about the role offers she received after winning an Oscar "Oh, Lupita, we\'d like you to play another movie where you\'re a slave, but this time, you\'re on a slave ship." pic.twitter.com/QUf9H6318E — Blackish Press (@blackishpress) November 22, 2025 Nyong’o added, “Those are the kind of offers I was getting in the months after winning my Academy Award.” The Us actress also called this a “tender time” as the media extrapolated on her Hollywood trajectory. Lupita Nyong’o is getting real about her acting career since winning an Oscar in 2013 for 12 Years A Slave . The acclaimed actress, who won the Academy Award for her captivating performance as enslaved woman Patsey, told CNN Inside Africa about how she only received offers for similar roles yet refused to play into the stereotypes. So, it really did set the paces for everything I’ve done since. She remained adamant about following her heart and mind by choosing roles she felt aligned with her values. She even called the moment immediately after winning a “very tender time.” “There is an expectation for you and your career,” she continued. “There were think pieces about, is this the beginning or the end of this African woman’s career? I had to deafen myself to all those pontificators because at the end of the day I am not a theory…I am an actual person. I like to be a joyful warrior for changing the paradigms of what it means to be African. If that means I work one less job a year to ensure that I am not perpetuating these stereotypes that are expected of people from my content, then let me do that.” She still starred in some Blockbuster hits such as Star Wars: The Force Awakens and Black Panther. However, fans also saw her take on more culturally-enriching roles in films like Queen of Katwe . However, Hollywood pressure still got to the Us actress. Last year, she told Trevor Noah on his What Now ? podcast about her subconscious decision to lose her Kenyan accent to appeal to the American film market. Her plight is a similar experience many Black actors in Hollywood have felt before. With pay gaps and a lack of opportunities besides stereotypical roles, Black actors have voiced the fight for just and equitable representation in films. More sure of her art and voice today, Nyong’o is reaffirming her pride in her Kenyan-Mexican identity and face as a Black actress in Hollywood. She will grace the big screen again in Christopher Nolan’s upcoming blockbuster adaptation of The Odyssey. Bassyonni 27 Nov 2025 Home News Sports Entertainment Tech Business Home Entertainment Lupita Nyong’o Celebrates Chadwick Boseman’s Regal Walk of Fame Star Entertainment Lupita Nyong’o Celebrates Chadwick Boseman’s Regal Walk of Fame Star Bassyonni ago 7 days On November 20, 2023, Chadwick Boseman will be honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, highlighting his substantial contributions to film and culture. This tribute comes more than three years after his untimely death on August 28, 2020, due to colon cancer at the age of 43. Lupita Nyong’o Reflects on Boseman’s Legacy Lupita Nyong’o, Boseman’s co-star in the groundbreaking film “Black Panther,” expressed her reverence for the actor. She remarked that having his star near the Dolby Theatre signifies a space of prominence for a true king. “It means it won’t be missed,” she stated, emphasizing the importance of his legacy. Cultural Impact of “Black Panther” “Black Panther,” released in January 2018, was a cultural phenomenon and the first superhero film to earn a Best Picture nomination at the Academy Awards. The film grossed over $1.3 billion globally, showcasing the significance of African representation in Hollywood. Release Date: January 2018 Box Office Gross: $1.3 billion Awards: First superhero film nominated for Best Picture Boseman portrayed T’Challa, the regal superhero from Wakanda, symbolizing strength and pride in African ancestry. His performances as historical figures, including Jackie Robinson and Thurgood Marshall, further showcased his depth as an actor. Boseman’s Private Struggles and Public Philanthropy Boseman kept his battle with cancer private. Many of his colleagues, including Nyong’o and director Ryan Coogler, were unaware of his condition. Despite the challenges he faced, Boseman continued to work on significant projects, leaving an indelible mark on the film industry. Outside his film performances, Boseman was known for his charitable work. He visited pediatric cancer patients even while fighting his own illness, demonstrating his commitment to helping others. Commemoration and Memorials In recognition of his contributions, several memorials have been established. Howard University has reestablished its school of fine arts in Boseman’s name, and a performing arts academy in his hometown, Anderson, South Carolina, also honors him. The upcoming Hollywood Walk of Fame star will serve as another location for fans and admirers to pay their respects. Photo: AP You have probably heard his name many times this past week on social media or the news – but if you missed it, 34-year-old Zohran Mamdani recently won New York City’s mayoral election after a smart, engaging, long-running campaign. Given the buzz surrounding his historic rise to be the Big Apple’s new mayor, a lot of stories and claims have emerged. One of these claims is that Mamdani was once a rapper before entering politics. Is this true? VERDICT: TRUE Yes, this is true. Mamdani pursued rapping as a career for a time as “Young Cardamom” which later became “Mr Cardamom.” He released his first song in 2016, collaborating with Ugandan rapper HAB on “Kanda (Chap Chap)”, a track about chapatti that became a local hit. They then released an EP titled “Sidda Mukyaalo” - translated as "No going back to the village" - which explored themes of postcolonial identity and multicultural belonging. Nani, released in 2019, was his final single before entering politics. The song was a tribute to his grandmother, Praveen Nair. On rapping, Mamdani said that music was his way to explore heritage and belonging. Aside from music, Mamdani also worked as a music supervisor on his mother Mira Nair’s 2016 film “Queen of Katwe” which starred Lupita Nyong’o and David Oyelowo.
